recommendedTextbook.title: Essential Geography for Senior Secondary Schools
recommendedTextbook.author: O. A. Iwena
recommendedTextbook.approvedBy: NERDC & Lagos State Ministry of Basic Education

topics.topic: Map Work: Contours and Topographic Landforms
subtopics: Interpretation of contour lines: Uniform slope, concave slope, convex slope, stepped slope
Landforms on 1:50,000 maps: Valleys, spurs, cols, ridges, knolls, plateaus, cliffs, escarpments
Intervisibility between two points and gradient calculation (Vertical Interval / Horizontal Equivalent)
objectives: Identify 6 standard relief features represented by contour patterns on topographical sheets
Calculate topographical gradient between two spot heights
Draw a cross-sectional relief profile between two given points on a WAEC map

topics.topic: Weather, Climate and Elements of the Atmosphere
subtopics: Meteorological instruments: Stevenson screen, maximum and minimum thermometer, hygrometer, barometer, wind vane, anemometer, rain gauge
Factors influencing world climates: Latitude, altitude, continentality, ocean currents, prevailing winds
objectives: Describe the construction and placement rules of a standard meteorological Stevenson screen
Calculate mean monthly temperature, annual temperature range, and total annual rainfall from climatic tables
Explain why Jos Plateau experiences cooler temperatures than surrounding northern lowlands

topics.topic: Hydrological Cycle and River Action Landforms
subtopics: Processes of the hydrological cycle: Evaporation, evapotranspiration, condensation, precipitation, runoff, infiltration
Stages of a river course: Youth/upper course (V-shaped valleys, waterfalls, gorges)
Mature/middle course (meanders, river cliffs) and old/lower course (ox-bow lakes, braided channels, deltas)
objectives: Diagram the closed hydrological water cycle with all transfer and storage pathways
Explain the hydraulic mechanisms of river erosion (corrasion, attrition, solution, hydraulic action)
Describe the developmental stages of an ox-bow lake using progressive diagrams

topics.topic: Action of Wind and Water in Arid Regions
subtopics: Wind erosion mechanisms: Deflation and abrasion
Erosional landforms in deserts: Rock pedestals, zeugens, yardangs, inselbergs, deflation hollows
Wind deposition features: Barchan dunes, seif dunes, loess deposits
objectives: Distinguish wind deflation from wind abrasion
Draw and label a typical zeugen and yardang illustrating differential rock hardness
Explain the asymmetric cross-section and crescent shape of a sand barchan dune
